learningObjective: Diagnose a launch-overhead-limited workload from an Nsight Systems timeline showing many small kernels with large CPU-side gaps.

canonicalClaims.claim: When wall-time analysis shows short kernel durations (comparable to or less than the CPU-side gap between launches) and no other stalls (I/O, PCIe), the workload is launch-overhead limited; mitigations reduce launch count (fusion, torch.compile), amortize per-launch cost (CUDA Graphs), or increase per-kernel work.
conditions: The Nsight timeline attributes the wall-time gap to CPU-side dispatch rather than synchronization waits.
No large tensor transfers or dataloader stalls appear in the same interval.
nonImplications: Does not imply that CUDA Graphs are always applicable; workloads with variable shapes or Python control flow may not translate cleanly.
Does not imply that fusion always speeds a workload up; over-fusion can increase register pressure or hurt occupancy.

misconceptions.claim: Any workload with GPU utilization < 100% is memory-bandwidth-bound.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Sub-100% GPU utilization can be caused by launch overhead, PCIe transfers, dataloader stalls, or synchronization; not exclusively HBM saturation.

misconceptions.claim: Adding math to each kernel (increasing arithmetic intensity) resolves launch-overhead-limited workloads.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Adding math per kernel does not shrink the number of launches; only fusion, CUDA Graphs, or larger batches reduce launch overhead.

misconceptions.claim: Quantization reduces launch overhead because smaller tensors dispatch faster.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Quantization reduces memory footprint per kernel; the CPU-side dispatch cost per launch is largely independent of tensor size.

misconceptions.claim: The dataloader is always the primary cause of GPU idle time.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Dataloader stalls are one of several possible causes; Nsight timelines usually distinguish CPU-side dispatch gaps from CPU-side dataloader waits.

implementationFacts: Typical CUDA launch overhead: 5-20 µs on host-side, higher with additional synchronization
CUDA Graphs replay a captured sequence with a single dispatch, amortizing per-launch cost
torch.compile via TorchInductor typically reduces launch count by fusing pointwise chains
performanceScenarios: Small-batch training or single-batch inference on modern GPUs often exposes launch overhead; the same model at large batch size becomes compute-bound instead.
